chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him about wiping over the feet, and he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْإِسْنَادِ: the chain of narrators transmitting the hadith
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ: wiping, here referring to the act performed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ: peace be upon them both, an honorific for the Imams عليهما السلام
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is unobjectionable or permissible in this context

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about wiping over the feet in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a brief legal ruling concerning wiping over the feet in wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام responds permissively, indicating that this act presents no problem within the discussed context.
